title: Backtesting and scores
text: Deaths populations England sex deprivation quintile, 2001-2019 (ONS). Three models, chosen examples: random walk drift per age (rwd()): log rate continues average change past. standard benchmark forecasting: model beat adds little; Lee-Carter (lee_carter()), one model per stratum; Li-Lee (li_lee(common_by = "sex")), quintiles sex pooled around common trend.
code: library(mortensor) library(data.table) x <- mt_data(deaths = ons_data, population = ons_data, by = c("sex", "imd_decile"), age = "age_group",              value = c(deaths = "all_causes", population = "population")) x <- mt_as_exposure(x, type = "midyear") x <- mt_group_levels(x, "imd_decile", function(d) paste0("Q", ceiling(as.numeric(d) / 2)), name = "quintile") models <- list("random walk" = rwd(), "Lee-Carter" = lee_carter(), "Li-Lee" = li_lee(common_by = "sex"))

title: Bayesian age-period-cohort models with bamp
text: mcmc_control("fast") runs four chains 5,000 iterations (burn-1,000, thinning 5). wrapper checks convergence bamp::checkConvergence() refits longer chains needed; stratum converge reported failed instead used. default priors second-order random walk age first-order random walks period cohort (see “Choice priors” ). Posterior medians 90% credible intervals effects (logit scale, identified bamp’s convention), Gelman-Rubin statistics chains (rhat, 1.1 converged):
code: prep <- mt_prep(step_ungroup()) set.seed(1) t0 <- proc.time() fit <- mt_fit(apc_bayes(mcmc = mcmc_control("fast")), x, prep = prep) (proc.time() - t0)[["elapsed"]] #> [1] 174.176 fit$diagnostics #>    stratum status                              message seconds #> 1:  female     ok                                       86.849 #> 2:    male     ok exposures rounded (max change 0.002)  83.735 eff <- mt_parameters(fit) eff[, .N, by = .(stratum, parameter)] #>    stratum parameter  N #> 1:  female       age 13 #> 2:  female    period 37 #> 3:  female    cohort 97 #> 4:    male       age 13 #> 5:    male    period 37 #> 6:    male    cohort 97 #> 7:  female      rhat  4 #> 8:    male      rhat  4 eff[parameter == "rhat", .(stratum, index, rhat = round(value, 3))] #>    stratum       index  rhat #> 1:  female    age_prec 1.000 #> 2:  female period_prec 1.001 #> 3:  female cohort_prec 1.000 #> 4:  female      fitted 1.003 #> 5:    male    age_prec 1.000 #> 6:    male period_prec 1.000 #> 7:    male cohort_prec 1.001 #> 8:    male      fitted 1.004 ggplot2::ggplot(eff[parameter != "rhat"], ggplot2::aes(as.numeric(index), value, colour = stratum, fill = stratum)) +   ggplot2::geom_ribbon(ggplot2::aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +   ggplot2::geom_line() +   ggplot2::facet_wrap(~parameter, scales = "free") +   ggplot2::labs(x = "Index (age group, period or cohort)", y = "Effect (logit scale)", colour = NULL, fill = NULL) +   scale_colour_mortensor(type = "categorical") +   scale_fill_mortensor(type = "categorical") +   theme_mortensor()

title: Inequality in England: life expectancy and causes of death by deprivation
text: Deaths mid-year populations sex, 5-year age group decile Index Multiple Deprivation, England 2001-2019 (ons_data; Source: Office National Statistics, Open Government Licence v3.0), combined quintiles (Q1 deprived, Q5 least deprived): hierarchy. ten series sex quintile add England sexes. forecasts made ten series summed (reconciled(method = "bottom_up")), England sum quintiles every path (“Coherent forecasts: totals parts”): observed gap life expectancy birth Q5 Q1:  women gap widened 5.2 years 2001 6.5 years 2019, 2011. men stayed 7.5 years, dip around 2010.
code: x <- mt_data(deaths = ons_data, population = ons_data, by = c("sex", "imd_decile"), age = "age_group",              value = c(deaths = "all_causes", population = "population")) x <- mt_as_exposure(x, type = "midyear") x <- mt_group_levels(x, "imd_decile", function(d) paste0("Q", ceiling(as.numeric(d) / 2)), name = "quintile") mt_validate(x) #> <mt_validation> no findings h <- mt_hierarchy(sex = "both", quintile = list(total = "England")) xa <- mt_aggregate_strata(x, h) bu <- function(model) reconciled(model, h, method = "bottom_up") gap_obs <- mt_contrast(xa, var = "quintile", ref = "Q1") mt_plot_contrast(observed = gap_obs, levels = "Q5")

code: set.seed(42) ages <- c("unter 1 Jahr", "1 bis unter 5 Jahre", paste(seq(5, 85, 5), "bis unter", seq(10, 90, 5), "Jahre"),           "90 Jahre und mehr") lo <- c(0, 1, seq(5, 90, 5)) g <- CJ(Jahr = 2005:2022, Geschlecht = 1:2, Quintil = 1:5, k = seq_along(ages)) g[, Altersgruppe := ages[k]] g[, bev := round(4e4 * exp(-lo[k] / 45) * (1 + 0.1 * (Quintil == 1)))] g[, rate := exp(-10.1 + 0.09 * (lo[k] + 2) + 0.3 * (Geschlecht == 1) + 0.12 * (5 - Quintil) - 0.015 * (Jahr - 2005))] g[k == 1, rate := 0.004] g[Jahr %in% 2020:2022, rate := rate * 1.12]                 # pandemic years g[, Gestorbene := rpois(.N, bev * pmin(rate, 0.7))] deaths <- g[, .(Jahr, Geschlecht, Quintil, Altersgruppe,                 Gestorbene = ifelse(Gestorbene == 0, "-", ifelse(Gestorbene < 3, ".", Gestorbene)))] totals <- g[, .(Altersgruppe = "Insgesamt", Gestorbene = as.character(sum(Gestorbene))),             by = .(Jahr, Geschlecht, Quintil)] deaths <- rbind(deaths, totals) pop <- g[, .(Stichtag = Jahr, Geschlecht, Quintil, Altersgruppe, Bevoelkerung = bev)] pop <- rbind(pop[Stichtag == 2005][, Stichtag := 2004], pop)   # 31 December of the year before f_deaths <- file.path(tempdir(), "gestorbene.csv") f_pop <- file.path(tempdir(), "bevoelkerung.csv") fwrite(deaths, f_deaths, sep = ";") fwrite(pop, f_pop, sep = ";")

title: Smoothing death rates
text: mt_smooth() smooths one three directions: age, year separately (Poisson P-splines): removes noise neighbouring ages, keeps every year observed; open interval 90+ expanded single years, exposure split PCLM exposures, mt_ungroup(); time, age separately (weighted Whittaker smoothing log rates, deaths weights): removes year--year variation, keeps age pattern every year; age-period surface (quasi-Poisson additive model tensor-product spline te(age, year), package mgcv): .  points observed rates women Q1. Smoothing age leaves almost year--year variation, 5-year age groups neighbouring ages already agree closely; matters single years age sparse data (small areas, causes death). Smoothing time surface remove year--year variation keep trend, including end decline 2011. time, smoothing parameter chosen age: 85-89, deaths many year--year variation large relative Poisson noise, smoother keeps much variation.
code: sm <- list("over age" = mt_smooth(x),            "over time" = mt_smooth(x, along = "period", method = "whittaker"),            "age-period surface" = mt_smooth(x, dims = 2, method = "gam")) mt_plot_smooth(x, sm, ages = c("45-49", "65-69", "85-89"), strata = "female.Q1")

Small values mean annual variation removed. age, dispersion 1.5: around spline, deaths neighbouring age groups vary little Poisson noise. time observed deaths vary twice much Poisson noise around trend (1.9), around surface three times much (3.3): years differ chance, smoothing treats year effects noise. surface removes year--year variation (trend_ratio 0.046, 0.167 time); smoother time follows ages many deaths closely, figure showed 85-89. One two Bayesian core models describes ROMIs every age years base period: core = "exponential" (core model paper's applications): rho[x, t] ~ N(exp(b1[x] + b2[x] log t), sigma^2), b1[x] ~ N(theta1[x], sigma1^2), b2[x] ~ N(theta2[x], sigma2^2), theta1[x] theta2[x] least-squares estimates log rho[x, t] = theta1[x] + theta2[x] log t age sigma, sigma1, sigma2 uniform (0, 1). Improvements can level ; mortality increases forecast. core = "linear": rho[x, t] ~ N(b1[x] + b2[x] t, sigma^2) (b1[x], b2[x]) bivariate normal means mu1, mu2 covariance standard deviations omega1, omega2 correlation r; uniform priors sigma, omega1, omega2 (0, 1), mu1, mu2 (-0.1, 0.1) r (-1, 1). Trends improvements continue linearly. posterior future ROMIs (one curve posterior sample plus normal noise sample's sigma) sampled Markov chain Monte Carlo. Forecast ROMIs outside limits set nearest limit (paper uses 0.005 0.035: mortality declines least 0.5% 3.5% year; excludes implausible forecasts "setting thresholds", package reads setting values thresholds). Death rates follow last smoothed rates base period m[x, t] = m[x, t - 1] (1 - rho[x, t - 1]) (equation 20). draws = "quantiles" (paper's method) draw j n applies quantile (j - 0.5) / n forecast ROMIs every age year, draws give quantiles death rates paper. draws comonotone across ages years; order permuted random, draws different strata independent. draws = "samples" (package-specific) every draw path one posterior sample noise. paths give much narrower intervals summary measures life expectancy, yearly noise improvements averages ages years. defaults follow paper's application (Table 3): exponential core model, five chains 5,200 iterations first 200 discarded every fifth kept (5,000 samples), limits 0.005 0.035. paper recommends base period least long forecast horizon, uses single years age 0. differs paper. paper samples JAGS; sampler written package used (Metropolis steps curve parameters age, proposals scaled curvature least-squares estimates adapted burn-; conjugate draws variances truncated prior range; moves scale sigma1 sigma2 together deviations curve parameters theta; Gibbs slice sampling steps linear core model). paper state following, choices package (package-specific, reference unknown): time t counts years base period 1 (change first second year) continues forecast; ROMIs lower limit (0.001 limits = NULL lower limit 0 ) set limit least-squares fit theta (paper sets negative values "minimum greater zero"); P-spline surface cubic B-splines knots every 5 years age time second-order penalties, smoothing parameters chosen BIC (paper uses package MortalitySmooth); grid starts age 0 interval, rates age 0 smoothed time (mt_smooth() leaves first year life); forecast ROMIs kept 1 rates stay positive. model's option let population converge mortality trend reference populations, weights shift population references forecast years, implemented: paper leaves weighting scheme open. stratum forecast data. title: mortensor: flexible mortality forecasting across data granularities — mortensor-package
text: Data: mt_data() stores deaths, exposures populations observed age period resolution (age_groups(), single_ages(), single_years(), parse_age_labels()); as_mt_data() mt_from_hmd() read Human Mortality Database data; mt_validate() checks plausibility; mt_example() simulates data known truth. Harmonisation: mt_regroup() aggregates exactly, mt_ungroup() estimates single-year data penalized composite link model, mt_smooth() smooths rates; mt_prep() bundles steps backtests refit every training window. Models: rwd(), lee_carter(), p_splines(), cp_splines(), arima_series(), ets_series(), hyndman_ullah(), coherent_fdm(), stmomo() (including Plat model), stanmomo(), li_lee(), coda(), bohk_rau(), nordpred_apc(), apc_bayes() (package bamp), experimental tucker3() coda_causes(), ensemble(), fitted mt_fit() (optionally tuned tuned()) forecast mt_forecast() simulated paths (mt_draws). product_ratio() cause_shares() deprecated. article "Methods sources" lists published source every method. Hierarchies: mt_hierarchy() describes crossed nested strata (example sex x region x deprivation quintile totals), mt_aggregate_strata() adds aggregates, mt_reconcile() reconciled() make forecasts add draw draw, mt_order_strata() imposes orderings. Wrappers model: ensemble(), reconciled(), recalibrated() (spread fitted recent forecast errors), anchored() (jump-observed level), bootstrapped() tuned(). Evaluation: mt_backtest() mt_score(), rates, life expectancy age-standardised rates. past: mt_observed(), mt_contrast() mt_inequality(). Derived quantities plots: life_table(), life_expectancy(), mt_deaths(), mt_plot_forecast() mt_plot_*() functions. Decomposition: mt_decompose() splits differences life expectancy summaries age, cause subgroup composition, observed data, forecasts .

text: Steps: step_ungroup(...): mt_ungroup(), default published PCLM without rescaling group totals (models fitted ungrouped data backtest scores grouped test data need exact group totals); step_ungroup(preserve_totals = TRUE) rescales; step_smooth(...): mt_smooth(). model fitted smoothed rates; residuals observation noise refer raw deaths. Smoothing time (along = "period", dims = 2) narrows forecast intervals models period index, check coverage backtest consider recalibrated(); step_regroup(age, period): mt_regroup(); step_grid(age, period): mt_set_grid(); step_window(years): keeps last years years training data, fitting period chosen relative forecast origin (example change trend; compare windows tuned() mt_backtest()); step_shocks(periods, action): periods exceptional mortality (example 2020-2022) either replaced log-linear interpolation rates neighbouring periods ("interpolate", deaths become exposure times interpolated rate, provenance "interpolated") removed ("exclude", start end data). "interpolate", shock periods start end data, neighbour one side, removed instead, warning class mt_warning_prep (backtest whose training window ends inside shock). interpolated years enter fit observed: model sees straight line log rates neighbouring years, without year--year variation observed years. Models estimate uncertainty year--year changes (example random walk period index) therefore estimate smaller variance, forecast intervals become narrower; check coverage backtest. Excluding periods (possible edges) avoids .

title: Generalised age-period-cohort models (StMoMo) — stmomo
text: Wrapper around StMoMo (Villegas, Kaishev Millossovich 2018): age-period-cohort ("apc"), Cairns-Blake-Dowd ("cbd", logit link), Renshaw-Haberman ("rh"), M6, M7 M8 ("m6", "m7", "m8", logit link), Plat model ("plat", logit link) Lee-Carter ("lc"). "rh" StMoMo's Renshaw-Haberman model cohortAgeFun = "1" (default StMoMo's rh()): log m(x,t) = (x) + b(x) k(t) + g(t - x), cohort effect without age modulation, original 2006 specification Renshaw-Haberman model, whose cohort effect modulated second age function. Models fitted per stratum real ages (lower bounds single-year intervals; models cohort effect need single years age), deaths central exposures; logit-link models initial exposures approximated central exposures plus half deaths, forecast death probabilities converted central rates (m = -log(1 - q)). Cohorts observed fewer clip cells get zero weight; fitted rates use effect nearest estimated cohort. title: mortensor 0.1.9000 (development of 0.2.0)
text: Work package E4. full texts papers earlier available abstracts read (sources access dev/methods-audit.md), implementations follow . Results change. Corrected papers: coda() follows Bergeron-Boucher et al. (2017): time index ARIMA(0,1,1) drift (random walk order = c(0, 1, 0)), common component coherent model comes mean death rates, deviations ARIMA(1,1,0), rates age 80 Kannisto model age 120 (open = "auto"; regression open interval open = "regression"), intervals come paper’s residual bootstrap. Fitted values point forecasts reproduce authors’ code 1e-9. 95% coverage England & Wales men 0.888 (0.981 ); French women coherent model accurate (CRPS 0.0743 0.0764; open interval 0.039 0.062). coda_causes() rank, order drift (Oeppen 2008 used rank 2 ARIMA(0,2,2)); tucker3() uses ranks Russolillo, Giordano Haberman (2011), c(2, 2, 2), reports fit measure. Non-negative reconciliation algorithm Wickramasuriya, Turlach Hyndman (2020); former heuristic, miss optimum, removed. MinT fixed nodes, nodes take covariances conditional fixed nodes. Results agree quadratic program 4e-10. life_table(open = "kannisto"/"gompertz") fits closure maximum likelihood, Thatcher, Kannisto Vaupel (1998); published parameters reproduced within 0.11%, former least-squares fit 82%. coherent_fdm() uses weighted principal components (weighted = TRUE, beta = 0.05), Hyndman, Booth Yasmeen (2013): CRPS France 0.0550 0.0596, 95% coverage 0.802 0.760. mt_ungroup(open_split = "pclm") (default): exposure open grid interval split PCLM exposures, Rizzi, Gampe Eilers (2015); stationary split open_split = "stationary". mt_dm_test(): equal-weighted cosine variance Lazarus et al. (2018); varestimator = "daniell" gives test Coroneo Iacone (2020), oversized overlapping test years. New published models: p_splines(): two-dimensional Poisson P-spline forecasting (Currie, Durban Eilers 2004), adapted MortalitySmooth 2.3.4, whose fitted forecast rates reproduces 1e-11. England & Wales men CRPS 0.035 0.071 Lee-Carter; life-expectancy intervals narrow (95% coverage 0.40). cp_splines(): smooth constrained mortality forecasting (Camarda 2019), P-spline forecasts asymmetric penalties rates ageing change; reproduces author’s code 2e-11. French women CRPS 0.066 0.085 Lee-Carter; intervals hold fit uncertainty , paper. bohk_rau(): varying age-specific survival improvements (Bohk-Ewald Rau 2017), Bayesian, paper’s forecast limits quantile draws. England & Wales men CRPS 0.045 (linear core 0.043) 0.071 Lee-Carter, 95% coverage life expectancy 30 0.90. stmomo("plat"): Plat (2009) model specified StMoMo vignette (Villegas, Kaishev Millossovich 2018); CRPS 3% Lee-Carter ages 55-89. nordpred_apc(): Nordpred age-period-cohort model power link cut trend (Møller et al. 2003), written mortensor; projections agree nordpred package 3e-8. draws hold coefficient uncertainty far narrow (95% coverage 0.11). Fixes: quantiles draws interpolated + w (b - ), tied draws longer give median upper quantile; errors rejected candidate models forecast package longer appear knitted documents coherent_fdm(). Documentation: dev/generalisation-plan.md plans experimental generalisations deprecated package methods, grounded verified literature.
